gallery.alt: Interference is a range–frequency structure. First isolate interference from spherical spreading: this continuous analytic contour divides the coherent direct-plus-pressure-release image transfer by the direct-path transfer. Source/receiver depths are 8/12 m, c = 1500 m/s, surface coefficient −1. Blue bands are cancellation, red bands reinforcement; white is 0 dB relative to direct, not zero pressure. The logarithmic range axis spans 25–500 m. This is an independently evaluated continuous two-ray reference, not the discrete propagator, receiver FIR, or a ray-traced ocean model. Values below −45 dB saturate.

gallery.alt: Direct path, reflection and receiver response. Read the upper panel as complex pressure addition: reflected and direct magnitudes are nearly coincident at 100 m, but the reflected path carries a sign reversal and a different delay. Their coherent sum has deep notches; adding magnitude curves would miss them. Gains reference the nominal 1 m source pressure. The lower panel is computed from the actual generic receiver coefficients, not a measured instrument: 257-tap Kaiser FIR, 10 kHz cutoff and 128/48000 s group delay. The continuous channel does not include fractional-delay interpolation error; the receiver is a separate operation.

Then compare the receiver in Pa (a separate, per-case amplitude axis). Each vertical stroke retains a block minimum and maximum; it is not decimated point sampling. figures.alt: 2 · Separate propagation, receiver and noise. Next separate the spectrum into source, pre-filter channel, clean filtered signal, filtered noise and their actual sum. The sum PSD includes finite-record cross terms; it is not manufactured by adding the two component PSDs. All cases share frequency/level axes. Welch: 2048-sample periodic Hann, 1024 overlap, segment-mean removal, one-sided Pa²/Hz; source uses only emission and receiver uses its metadata window. Spectral dB = 10 log10(PSD / 10⁻¹² Pa²/Hz); displayed 0–12 kHz and −90–115 dB, with a −120 dB computational display floor only. Exact full-Nyquist linear spectra are downloadable. Welch window weighting is not the full-record RMS convention.

figures.alt: 3 · Read the time–frequency signature. Finally ask when each frequency occurs. These are density spectrograms, not independently normalized pictures: source and receiver, and every passive case, share −20 to 100 dB re 1 µPa²/Hz. Values outside this display interval saturate; exact linear matrices are supplied separately. Frames use 512-sample periodic Hann windows, 384 overlap, per-frame mean removal, no padding; times are frame centres on the emission clock. Source frames lie inside the unpadded emission; receiver frames lie inside its analysis window. Blank regions have no complete frame, not measured silence. The receiver delay, coloration and noise are not removed to improve appearance.
